history.summary: A 12th-century Shaivite temple dedicated to Gokarneshvara, an aspect of Shiva, commissioned by the Chahamana king Vigraharaja IV, also known as Bisal Deo or Visala Deva (r. c. 1150-1164 CE), who also founded the town (earlier Vigrahapura/Bisalpur/Visalpur). A Monument of National Importance (ASI, restored by the Jaipur Circle). The temple drew its sacrality from a much older Gokarna cave shrine nearby, whose svayambhu linga was worshipped before the structural temple; contemporaneous inscriptions (1174 CE, 1187 CE under Prithviraja Chauhan) call it the shrine of Gokarna Deva. The courtyard is partly submerged by the Bisalpur Dam reservoir at high water levels; before the dam (1990s) the temple stood atop a hill overlooking the confluence of the Banas and Dai rivers. FLAG: CSV town 'Tonk' is the district, not the location - the temple is at the village of Bisalpur, Deoli tehsil, ~80 km from Tonk town.

name: Bisaldeo (Gokarneswar) Temple, Bisalpur
town: Bisalpur (CSV says Tonk; actual site is the village of Bisalpur, Tonk district)
town_description: Bisalpur is a village in Deoli tehsil of Tonk district, Rajasthan, on the Banas River at the Bisalpur Dam (completed 1999), about 150 km from Jaipur. Known for the dam reservoir, the 12th-century Bisaldeo temple and the older Gokarna cave shrine, it is an offbeat heritage and pilgrimage spot.
tradition: Shaivite (Gokarneshvara; ASI-protected monument with living worship)

travel.railway: Tonk has no railway station; nearest major railheads Jaipur (~150 km) and Sawai Madhopur (~120 km, verify)
travel.road: On SH 37A near Bisalpur Dam; ~80 km from Tonk town by road (verify)

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Maha Shivaratri draws thousands. Note the courtyard may be submerged when reservoir levels are high.
visitor_information.opening_hours: ASI monument; typically accessible sunrise-sunset - verify locally
